label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
## Proposal: Set a January 15 intake date for H-1B registrations

**Decision needed Thursday** so engagement letters can go out the week of December 7.

Last season (March 2026) we filed 14 registrations for 6 employer clients, and 9 of those 14 came in during the final week of February. Rosa logged about 11 hours of overtime the week the window opened. That wasn't really about clients being slow. We send the questionnaire whenever an employer asks for it, so nobody ever had a date to work toward. One HR contact told me she'd have happily sent everything in January if we'd asked. I think most of the crunch comes from our own process, and we can fix that.

An earlier date also protects us. The registration itself is simple, but mistakes are expensive. A wrong or expired passport can make a selection invalid. Last season one beneficiary's passport scan arrived two days before the window, and it had expired in October. We only caught it because Rosa checked the dates. I don't want to rely on catches like that during the busiest week of the year.

January 15 seems realistic. HR teams are back from the holidays by then and have their budgets set. Employers already plan for the $215-per-beneficiary registration fee in Q1, so we aren't asking them to move money around. We're just giving them a clear date and making it easier to get things to us.

**What would change:**

- **Week of December 7:** engagement letters and a one-page questionnaire go to all cap-season clients
- **January 15:** intake closes
- **After January 15:** anything that comes in late is handled case by case, not turned away
- **January 15 to the window:** Rosa, who owns the tracker, gets a clean six weeks to chase missing documents, check passport dates, and follow up on gaps before we file

I'd pitch this to clients as better service. They get a predictable timeline, fewer last-minute requests from us, and more time for us to catch problems before they cost anyone a selection. If we agree Thursday, I'll draft the December letter and questionnaire that week so Rosa can look them over.

---

I left out Brightwater's name on purpose. In a doc that might get passed around, naming them could read as calling them out. You can add it back if you'd rather.
